message.content: {"rules":["`self` must be valid for reads.","`self` must be valid for writes.","`self` must be properly aligned, even if `T` has size 0.","`self` must be nonnull, even if `T` has size 0.","The value pointed to by `self` must be valid for dropping, including any additional invariants required by its type.","While `self.drop_in_place()` is executing, parts of the value pointed to by `self` may be accessed only through the `&mut self` references supplied to the `Drop::drop` methods it invokes.","If `T` is not `Copy`, using the pointed-to value after calling `self.drop_in_place()` can cause undefined behavior; assignment through `*self = foo` counts as such a use because it drops the value again.","After calling `self.drop_in_place()`, `ptr::write` may be used to overwrite the pointed-to storage without dropping the old value, provided the destination remains valid for writes and properly aligned, even for a zero-sized `T`.","`drop_in_place` must be used to drop unsized types, such as trait objects, which cannot be read onto the stack and dropped normally.","`self.drop_in_place()` may be used to drop pinned data when `T` is not `repr(packed)`.","Pinned data must not be moved before it is dropped.","Unaligned values cannot be dropped in place; they must first be copied to an aligned location using `ptr::read_unaligned`. For fields of packed structs, the compiler performs this move automatically."]}
